security_audit.summary: All 35 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, ordinary Dart syntax, and an intentional public API example. One low-severity semantic concern remains because the example places a bearer-token placeholder directly in source code.

remediation.suggestion: Show tokens arriving from secure runtime configuration or platform-backed secret storage, and warn against committing credentials.

content.value_statement: Flutter REST integrations require platform permissions, response validation, parsing, and clear UI states. This skill provides a structured implementation workflow using Dart's http package.
actual_capabilities: Adds the http package and required Android and macOS network permissions.
Implements GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE request patterns.
Maps JSON responses into strongly typed Dart models.
Moves expensive response parsing into a Flutter background isolate.
Connects asynchronous requests to loading, success, and error UI states.
limitations: It does not provide authentication, token refresh, or secure secret storage.
It does not define retries, timeouts, caching, or offline behavior.
The complete example demonstrates GET requests rather than every supported operation.
Platform guidance covers Android and macOS, not every Flutter target.

use_cases.title: Create a First API Screen
use_cases.description: Build a Flutter screen that fetches REST data and displays loading, success, and error states.

use_cases.title: Standardize Service Methods
use_cases.description: Apply consistent headers, status validation, JSON conversion, and typed return values across an application.

use_cases.title: Improve Parsing Performance
use_cases.description: Move large response parsing away from the UI isolate and preserve responsive rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch REST Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Flutter GET request for [endpoint], map the response to [model], and display loading, success, and error states.

prompt_templates.title: Submit JSON Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement a Flutter POST request to [endpoint] using [request fields], JSON headers, status validation, and a typed response.

prompt_templates.title: Build a REST Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Create typed GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE methods for [resource], with shared headers and explicit failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Large Responses
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [request method] to parse large JSON responses with compute, enforce safe typing, and integrate the result with FutureBuilder.

output_examples.input: Fetch a photo list from a REST endpoint without blocking Flutter rendering.
output: A typed Photo model maps each response item.
A top-level parser runs through compute in a background isolate.
FutureBuilder presents loading, data, and error states.

output_examples.input: Add a JSON POST operation for creating a user profile.
output: The request sends encoded profile fields with the JSON content type.
The method accepts the expected creation status and returns a typed profile.
Other statuses produce an explicit exception.

output_examples.input: Prepare a Flutter application for network access.
output_examples.output: The project includes the http dependency, Android Internet permission, and macOS network-client entitlements.

best_practices: Parse endpoint strings with Uri APIs and pass request headers explicitly.
Validate expected status codes before decoding response bodies.
Initialize request futures once when widget rebuilds must not repeat network calls.
anti_patterns: Do not return null for failed requests because error states become ambiguous.
Do not parse large responses on the UI isolate.
Do not place production tokens directly in application source.

faq.question: Which HTTP operations does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE patterns using Flutter's http package.

faq.question: Does it configure platform network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Android Internet permission and macOS network-client entitlements.

faq.question: How are response bodies converted?
faq.answer: Responses are decoded from JSON and mapped to strongly typed Dart objects through factory constructors.

faq.question: When should parsing use compute?
faq.answer: Use compute when large JSON responses could cause dropped frames or delayed interactions.

faq.question: Does it manage authentication securely?
faq.answer: No. It shows authorization headers but does not implement secret storage, login, or token refresh.

faq.question: Does it include retry and timeout policies?
faq.answer: No. Add retry limits, request timeouts, and cancellation behavior according to application requirements.
